```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

read_tab <- function(f) read_tsv(f, show_col_types = FALSE, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

# Bold the best value of each row; `lower` lists the metrics where lower is better,
# `skip` the rows left unstyled (e.g. raw bin counts, where more is not better)
bold_best <- function(tbl, df, cols, lower = character(), skip = character()) {
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(df))) {
    if (df$metric[i] %in% skip) next
    vals <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(unlist(df[i, cols])))
    if (all(is.na(vals)) || length(unique(na.omit(vals))) == 1) next
    best <- if (df$metric[i] %in% lower) min(vals, na.rm = TRUE) else max(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
    win <- cols[!is.na(vals) & vals == best]
    tbl <- tab_style(tbl, cell_text(weight = "bold"), cells_body(columns = all_of(win), rows = i))
  }
  tbl
}
```

# Setup

- **Data:** 29 river metagenomes (anonymised as `S01`–`S29`), assembled per sample with MEGAHIT; contigs ≥1.5 kb.
- **Binning:** seven binners per sample. Each binner's bins were scored with CheckM2, and the best binner of each family was selected (**COMEBin, MetaCAT, CONCOCT**). The selected binners are the input of every refiner below.
- **Quality:** standalone `checkm2 predict` on the final bins of each method.
- **Quality tiers** (completeness / contamination):

  | Tier | Completeness | Contamination |
  |---|---|---|
  | MQ50 | ≥50% | <10% |
  | MQ70 | ≥70% | <10% |
  | HQ | ≥90% | <5% |
  | NC | ≥95% | <5% |

# Refiners: metawrap2, DAS Tool and Binette

The refiners were run on the same three binners. Binette used its default contamination ceiling (10%).

```{r refiners}
ref <- read_tab("data/refiner_comparison.tsv")
cols <- c("metawrap2", "dastool", "binette")
labels <- c(
  final_bins = "Final bins",
  `mq50_bins (>=50/<10)` = "MQ50 bins",
  `mq70_bins (>=70/<10)` = "MQ70 bins",
  `hq90_bins (>=90/<5)` = "HQ bins",
  `nc95_bins (>=95/<5)` = "NC bins",
  mq70_mean_contamination = "MQ70: mean contamination (%)",
  hq90_mean_contamination = "HQ: mean contamination (%)",
  hq90_binned_Mb = "HQ: total size (Mb)",
  `samples_best_or_tied_mq70 (of 29)` = "Samples best or tied, MQ70 (of 29)",
  `samples_best_or_tied_hq90 (of 29)` = "Samples best or tied, HQ (of 29)",
  `best_single_binner_mq70 (sum of per-sample max)` = "Best single binner, MQ70 (sum of per-sample maxima)"
)
ref_tab <- ref |>
  filter(metric %in% names(labels)) |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = names(labels))) |>
  arrange(metric) |>
  mutate(metric = as.character(metric), label = labels[metric]) |>
  select(metric, label, all_of(cols))

ref_tab |>
  gt(rowname_col = "label") |>
  cols_hide(metric) |>
  cols_label(metawrap2 = "metawrap2", dastool = "DAS Tool", binette = "Binette") |>
  tab_header(title = "Refined bins, all 29 samples", subtitle = "Best value per row in bold") |>
  bold_best(ref_tab, cols,
    lower = c("mq70_mean_contamination", "hq90_mean_contamination"),
    skip = c("final_bins", "best_single_binner_mq70 (sum of per-sample max)")) |>
  tab_source_note("metawrap2: bin_refinement -c 70 -x 10 with GUNC; DAS Tool: --score_threshold -42; Binette: --min_completeness 50.")
```

- **Binette** recovers the most HQ and NC bins. It is best or tied for HQ in 26 of 29 samples.
- **metawrap2** gives the cleanest bins, but `-c 70` drops all bins between 50% and 70% completeness.
- **DAS Tool** keeps 3,438 bins, but most of them are below MQ50.
- **Small gain over a single binner:** all three refiners add only about 4–7% MQ70 bins over the best single binner of each sample (674).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Per-sample counts

```{r refiners-per-sample}
ps <- read_tsv("data/per_sample_refiners.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ps |>
  gt(rowname_col = "sample") |>
  tab_spanner("metawrap2", starts_with("metawrap2_")) |>
  tab_spanner("DAS Tool", starts_with("dastool_")) |>
  tab_spanner("Binette", starts_with("binette_")) |>
  cols_label_with(fn = \(x) x |> str_remove("^[a-z0-9]+_") |>
    recode(final_bins = "bins", mq50 = "MQ50", mq70 = "MQ70", hq90 = "HQ", nc95 = "NC")) |>
  data_color(columns = ends_with("_hq90"), rows = sample != "TOTAL", palette = "Greens") |>
  tab_style(cell_text(weight = "bold"), cells_body(rows = sample == "TOTAL"))
```
:::

# After Binette: Rosella refine vs GUNC

Binette was rerun with contamination allowed up to **20%**, which gave 857 bins in total; 100 of them were above 10%. Two follow-up steps were then compared. Both end with CheckM2 and a ≤10% contamination filter, then dereplication with Galah (70% completeness / 10% contamination).

- **Rosella refine:** reworks the contaminated bins.
- **GUNC:** removes the bins that GUNC's default verdict flags as chimeric, then the bins above 10% contamination.

```{r rosella-gunc}
rg <- read_tab("data/refine_comparison.tsv")
cols2 <- c("binette20_rosella", "binette20_gunc")
labels2 <- c(
  bins_after_refine_step = "Bins after the step",
  new_bins_from_refine_step = "New bins made by the step",
  `refined_mq70 (>=70/<10)` = "MQ70 bins",
  `refined_hq90 (>=90/<5)` = "HQ bins",
  `refined_nc95 (>=95/<5)` = "NC bins",
  `final_mags (Galah)` = "Dereplicated MAGs",
  final_hq90 = "Dereplicated HQ",
  final_nc95 = "Dereplicated NC",
  final_mean_completeness = "Dereplicated: mean completeness (%)",
  final_mean_contamination = "Dereplicated: mean contamination (%)",
  final_Mb = "Dereplicated: total size (Mb)"
)
rg_tab <- rg |>
  filter(metric %in% names(labels2)) |>
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = names(labels2))) |>
  arrange(metric) |>
  mutate(metric = as.character(metric), label = labels2[metric]) |>
  select(metric, label, all_of(cols2))

rg_tab |>
  gt(rowname_col = "label") |>
  cols_hide(metric) |>
  cols_label(binette20_rosella = "Rosella", binette20_gunc = "GUNC") |>
  tab_header(title = "Binette (≤20% contamination) followed by Rosella or GUNC",
             subtitle = "All 29 samples; best value per row in bold") |>
  tab_row_group("After dereplication (Galah)", rows = startsWith(metric, "final")) |>
  tab_row_group("Before dereplication", rows = !startsWith(metric, "final")) |>
  bold_best(rg_tab, cols2,
    lower = c("final_mean_contamination"),
    skip = c("bins_after_refine_step", "new_bins_from_refine_step"))
```

- **Rosella** split 57 contaminated bins into 160 new bins, but these are mostly fragments: mean completeness 24.6%, and only one reaches MQ70. The extra MAGs in the Rosella run mostly come from bins that GUNC calls chimeric.
- **GUNC** gives 29 fewer dereplicated MAGs (318 against 347), which are a little cleaner and have passed a chimerism check that CheckM2 cannot do. It also runs faster: about 36 min per sample on 10 threads, against about 1.5 h on 30 threads for Rosella.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Per-sample counts

```{r rosella-gunc-per-sample}
ps2 <- read_tsv("data/per_sample_rosella_vs_gunc.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
ps2 |>
  gt(rowname_col = "sample") |>
  tab_spanner("Rosella", starts_with("rosella_")) |>
  tab_spanner("GUNC", starts_with("gunc_")) |>
  cols_label_with(fn = \(x) x |> str_remove("^(rosella|gunc)_") |>
    recode(binette_bins = "Binette bins", refined_bins = "bins", refined_mq70 = "MQ70",
           refined_hq90 = "HQ", refined_nc95 = "NC", final_mags = "MAGs",
           final_hq90 = "MAGs HQ", final_nc95 = "MAGs NC")) |>
  data_color(columns = ends_with("final_hq90"), rows = sample != "TOTAL", palette = "Greens") |>
  tab_style(cell_text(weight = "bold"), cells_body(rows = sample == "TOTAL"))
```
:::

# Conclusions

- **Recommended setup:** Binette with contamination up to 20%, then GUNC, then a final ≤10% CheckM2 contamination filter before dereplication (PR #40).
- **Rosella refine isn't worth its compute:** it adds a single MAG for about 1.5 h on 30 threads per sample.

| `data/per_sample_refiners.tsv` | Per-sample bins and tiers for the three refiners |
| `data/per_sample_rosella_vs_gunc.tsv` | Per-sample bins, tiers and dereplicated MAGs for Rosella and GUNC |
